rationale: This mixed-methods provincial case study in Quang Ninh, Vietnam combines a questionnaire survey of 270 rural households, 14 in-depth interviews with district officials and water company technical staff, and provincial facility assessments (262 systems). Its primary governance exposure is regulatory_model_ownership, comparing rural water systems operated by joint-stock utilities, private enterprises, community cooperatives, and village water boards, while secondarily examining fees_tariffs_subsidies (cost-recovery criteria, household tariff levels vs willingness-to-pay, and proposed subsidies). For outcomes, effective_access (operational reliability, continuous supply, water quality compliance, and functional sustainability across facilities) is the primary focal outcome, alongside co-central empirical analyses of primary_connection (spatial disparities in piped water coverage rates) and economic_access (tariff affordability thresholds), warranting 'multiple' for assigned_outcome_label_with_multiple.
